Ta có $|e^x - 1| = \begin{cases} 1 - e^x, & x \in [-1;0] \\ e^x - 1, & x \in [0;1] \end{cases}$.\
		Suy ra $\displaystyle \int_{-1}^1 |e^x - 1|\,\mathrm{d}x = \displaystyle \int_{-1}^0 (1 - e^x)\,\mathrm{d}x + \displaystyle \int_0^1 (e^x - 1)\,\mathrm{d}x = (x - e^x)\Big|_{-1}^0 + (e^x - x)\Big|_0^1$.\
		$= (-1) - (-1 - e^{-1}) + (e - 1) - 1 = e + e^{-1} - 2$.\
		Vậy $a+b+c = 1 + 1 + (-2) = 0$.
